# Chiggers

Chiggers are tiny mite larvae that are common in many parts of the world, particularly in warm, humid environments.

## What They Are
- Larvae of mites in the family **Trombiculidae**
- Extremely small (less than 1/150 inch) - barely visible to the naked eye
- Red or orange in color
- Only the larval stage bites humans; adults feed on plant material

## Where They Live
- Tall grass, weeds, and brush
- Berry patches and woodland edges
- Most active in summer and early fall
- Common in the southern and midwestern United States

## How They Bite
- They **don't burrow into skin** (common misconception)
- They attach and inject enzymes that break down skin cells
- They feed on the dissolved tissue, not blood
- Usually fall off after a few days

## Symptoms
- Intense itching, often starting hours after exposure
- Red welts or bumps, sometimes with a white center
- Common around ankles, waistbands, and areas where clothing is tight

## Prevention & Treatment
- Wear long pants and use insect repellent (DEET or permethrin)
- Shower soon after outdoor activities
- Wash clothes in hot water
- Treat bites with anti-itch creams or antihistamines

The itching can last 1-2 weeks even after the chigger is gone.
